questions.stem: (i) Find the exact solutions to the equations

parts.label: i(a)
parts.mark_scheme: $\ln(3x-7)=5$. $\mathrm{e}^{\ln(3x-7)}=\mathrm{e}^5$ M1: Takes e of both sides of the equation. This can be implied by $3x-7=\mathrm{e}^5$. $3x-7=\mathrm{e}^5\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^5+7}{3}\{=51.804\ldots\}$ dM1: Then rearranges to make $x$ the subject. A1: Exact answer of $\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^5+7}{3}$.

parts.label: i(b)
parts.mark_scheme: $3^x\mathrm{e}^{7x+2}=15$. $\ln(3^x\mathrm{e}^{7x+2})=\ln 15$ M1: Takes ln (or logs) of both sides of the equation. $\ln 3^x+\ln\mathrm{e}^{7x+2}=\ln 15$ M1: Applies the addition law of logarithms. $x\ln 3+7x+2=\ln 15$ A1 oe. $x(\ln 3+7)=-2+\ln 15$ ddM1: Factorising out at least two $x$ terms on one side and collecting number terms on the other side. $x=\dfrac{-2+\ln 15}{7+\ln 3}\{=0.0874\ldots\}$ A1 oe: Exact answer of $\dfrac{-2+\ln 15}{7+\ln 3}$.

parts.label: ii(a)
parts.text:
(ii) The functions f and g are defined by
$\mathrm{f}(x)=\mathrm{e}^{2x}+3, \quad x\in\mathbb{R}$
$\mathrm{g}(x)=\ln(x-1), \quad x\in\mathbb{R}, \ x>1$
(a) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$ and state its domain.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: $\mathrm{f}(x)=\mathrm{e}^{2x}+3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$. $y=\mathrm{e}^{2x}+3\Rightarrow y-3=\mathrm{e}^{2x}$ M1: Attempt to make $x$ (or swapped $y$) the subject. $\Rightarrow \ln(y-3)=2x \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\ln(y-3)=x$ M1: Makes $\mathrm{e}^{2x}$ the subject and takes ln of both sides. Hence $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}\ln(x-3)$ A1 cao: $\frac{1}{2}\ln(x-3)$ or $\ln\sqrt{(x-3)}$ or $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(y)=\frac{1}{2}\ln(y-3)$ (see appendix). $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$: Domain: $x>3$ B1: Either $x>3$ or $(3,\infty)$ or Domain $>3$.

parts.label: ii(b)
parts.text:
(b) Find fg and state its range.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: $\mathrm{g}(x)=\ln(x-1)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $x>1$. $\mathrm{fg}(x)=\mathrm{e}^{2\ln(x-1)}+3\{=(x-1)^2+3\}$ M1: An attempt to put function g into function f.
